_amend_plan for RETRIEVAL_INSUFFICIENT sets force_retrieval=true; but the fallback planner ALREADY emitted RETRIEVE for retrieval-cued classifications, so the amended plan is fingerprint-identical to the current plan -> runner.py:282-287 terminates STALLED on the first replan round

when the amended plan instead differs (e.g. MATH/MIXED additions), two replan rounds exhaust max_replans=2 and the third round's pre-step budget guard reads usage['replans']=2 >= cap and terminates BUDGET_EXHAUSTED before any further step (budgets.exceeded priority order)

aggregate_consistency.note: SIMPLE+NONE+GENERAL rows take the fast path (classify.py:99-105) -> PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED; MULTI_STEP/OPEN_ENDED + resources NONE rows run a single-SYNTHESIZE fallback plan, verify_final yields verdict UNKNOWN (no tool results, no supplied chunks), and decide_status falls through to UNCERTAIN; retrieval-cued rows hit the STALLED/BUDGET_EXHAUSTED no-status paths. The three buckets sum to 80 and match the T24 aggregate exactly without opening any row.

root_cause_statement: The 4 unmatched T24 GENERAL rows carry status UNKNOWN solely because the frozen provider adapter (t23_protocol/provider.py:100) substitutes the literal 'UNKNOWN' whenever the executive runtime terminates without an evidence_status. Three runtime termination classes never assign one: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (three sites), STALLED, and _hard_fail (system errors). In the frozen production GENERAL context (no retriever, no registry, max_new_tokens=32), retrieval-cued general questions deterministically reach STALLED (fingerprint-identical replan) or BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (max_replans axis). The status is therefore an adapter-fallback placeholder for 'status absent', not an epistemic state; the runtime defect is that these termination paths bypass evidence-status assignment.

semantic_classification.note: UNKNOWN as a terminal capability status is an implementation defect (adapter fallback for a missing status). UNKNOWN as an internal axis value (classification axes, verify verdicts, provenance) is valid and out of scope. Normalization: every runtime terminal must carry a defined evidence status derived from its recorded signals.
